items.html:
Three structural opportunities stand out; none was benchmarked here.

  1. Preserve EBCM’s azimuthal blocks through the solve. Integration already skips unequal m pairs in ebcm.rs:220 and groups rows by order at ebcm.rs:292. However, it returns dense Q matrices, and the documented construction uses a full dense np.linalg.solve(q, q_regular) at ebcm.py:95. For complete degree-L bases, solving independent m blocks changes factorization arithmetic from O(L⁶) to O(L⁴), with smaller working memory. This is an asymptotic opportunity for high L, not a measured overall gain: wave evaluation may still dominate moderate cases. A paired Q/Q_regular operation could additionally share identical inner regular waves, surface sampling, and angular factors; today the documented workflow calls qmat twice.

  2. Make the existing S-matrix thin-illumination Krylov path genuinely matrix-free. It currently forms I−LU with a dense matrix product at solve.rs:22, before deciding to use GMRES at solve.rs:154. Thus skipping LU does not eliminate cubic assembly. Applying x−L(Ux) would replace that assembly with O(kN²p) work for k iterations and p incident fields. Important constraint: current invertibility certification uses the formed product; a matrix-free replacement needs an equally valid or more conservative certification and must preserve singular-system behavior. Scope is large, weakly coupled stacks with few illuminations—not full S-matrix composition, which deliberately uses a direct solve for 2N RHS at compose.rs:55.

  3. Keep planar layer channels compact beyond slab construction. The native stack already computes independent two-polarization channels at layers.rs:153. Python immediately expands them into dense matrices at _smatrix.py:1043; subsequent cascade and transfer/band operations use generic dense kernels at _smatrix.py:342, _smatrix.py:366, and periodic.rs:107. Preserving independent transverse-wavevector blocks could turn cubic downstream work into linear work in channel count for uncoupled planar structures. It cannot apply after a general patterned array couples those channels, and a normal-incidence two-port slab offers little benefit.

Already optimized, so do not present as new wins: EBCM parallel node evaluation, radial-function sharing, equal-m integration, value-only forward wave evaluation; compact native slab construction; reuse of composition factors in analytic pullbacks; thin-illumination GMRES; repeated-stack doubling.

Read-only source inspection only. No edits, tests, benchmarks, Git changes, pushes, or PR activity.
